+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|           COMPARATIVE CRIMINOLOGY LANDSCAPE                      |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  WHAT VARIES ACROSS NATIONS:                                     |
|  - Incarceration rates (40-600+ per 100,000)                     |
|  - Crime definitions (marijuana, sex work, defamation)           |
|  - Justice system models (adversarial vs. inquisitorial)         |
|  - Sentencing philosophy (rehabilitation vs. punishment)         |
|  - Victim rights                                                 |
|  - Police organization (centralized vs. local)                   |
|                                                                  |
|  WHAT IS RELATIVELY UNIVERSAL:                                   |
|  - Age-crime curve                                               |
|  - Male overrepresentation                                       |
|  - Property crime > violent crime in volume                      |
|  - Urban concentration                                           |
|  - Correlation between inequality and violent crime              |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+

DRUG POLICY SPECTRUM
  ====================

  PROHIBITION                    DECRIMINALIZATION
  (US model, traditional)        (Portugal, 2001)
  ==================             ================
  Possession is crime            Possession for personal
  Drug courts as safety          use: no criminal charge
  valve                          Administrative panel
  Criminal record for            Treatment offered
  possession                     No criminal record
  | |
  v v
  LEGALIZATION                   HARM REDUCTION
  (Cannabis: US states,          (Netherlands, Switzerland)
  Canada, Netherlands)           =======================
  ==================             Needle exchanges
  Regulated commercial           Safe injection sites
  sale                           Heroin prescription
  Tax revenue                    (Switzerland 1994)
  Criminal market reduction      Reduces disease, death;
  (partial; illicit markets      crime falls
  persist for untaxed)

  PORTUGAL MODEL RESULTS (20 years):
  - HIV infections among users fell dramatically
  - Drug-related deaths fell
  - Drug use did NOT increase (as feared)
  - Treatment uptake increased
  - No spillover legalization effect
